subject: maths
title: Position and Direction: Left and Right, Turns and Patterns
seo_title: Year 2 Position and Direction Worksheets: Left, Right, Clockwise and Anticlockwise Turns
standard_text: Order and arrange combinations of mathematical objects in patterns and sequences; use mathematical vocabulary to describe position, direction and movement, including movement in a straight line and distinguishing between rotation as a turn and in terms of right angles for quarter, half and three-quarter turns (clockwise and anti-clockwise).
meta_desc: Free Year 2 maths worksheets on position and direction: above, below, left, right and between, moving a robot on a grid, quarter, half and three-quarter turns clockwise and anticlockwise, and shape patterns. 100 questions with an answer key, following the National Curriculum.
key_big: Clockwise is the way clock hands turn. A quarter turn is 1 right angle, a half turn is 2 and a three-quarter turn is 3.
key_sub: When you move on a grid, count the moves, not the square you start on. When a robot faces down the page, its left is on the right of the page.
body_html:
Where is it?

We use position words to say where things are: above, below, on the left of, on the right of, between and next to.

Example

What is between the star and the sun?

The star and the sun are in the top row. The moon is in the middle.

Answer: the moon

Moving on a grid

A robot moves forwards or backwards in a straight line. Count the squares it moves. Do not count the square it starts on. The arrow on the robot shows which way it faces.

Turns

Clockwise is the way the hands on a clock turn. Anticlockwise is the other way. A quarter turn is a right angle, like the corner of a page.

TurnRight anglesYou end up facing
Quarter turn1to the side
Half turn2the opposite way
Three-quarter turn3the other side
Whole turn4the same way again
Example

An arrow points up. It makes a quarter turn clockwise. Which way does it point?

Clockwise goes up, right, down, left. One quarter turn from up is right.

Answer: right

Patterns

Find the part that repeats. Say the pattern out loud, then keep going.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Mixing up left and right when the robot faces down the pageTurn the page round so you face the same way as the robot
Mixing up clockwise and anticlockwiseClockwise is the way clock hands go
Thinking a half turn is a quarter turnA half turn makes you face the opposite way
Counting the start square as a moveCount the moves, not the squares you stand on
Starting the pattern again from the wrong shapeFind the part that repeats and say it out loud

faq.q: What do Year 2 children learn about position and direction?
faq.a: They use words like above, below, left, right and between, move in straight lines on a grid, and make quarter, half and three-quarter turns clockwise and anticlockwise. They also continue patterns of shapes.

faq.q: What is the difference between clockwise and anticlockwise?
faq.a: Clockwise is the way the hands on a clock turn. Anticlockwise is the opposite way.

faq.q: How many right angles are in a half turn?
faq.a: A half turn is 2 right angles. A quarter turn is 1 right angle, a three-quarter turn is 3 and a whole turn is 4.

faq.q: How can I help my child learn position and direction at home?
faq.a: Play games that give directions, such as “take 3 steps forwards, then make a quarter turn clockwise”, or hide a toy and describe where it is. A toy robot or a simple treasure map on squared paper works well.

sets.title: Position words: above, below, left, right and between

items.q: What is on the left of the heart?
items.e: Look to the left side of the page. On the left of the heart is the fish. The house is on the right.

items.q: The fish is next to two things. What are they?
items.e: Next to means right beside. On its left is the ball. On its right is the house.

items.q: What is just above the fish?
items.e: Look up from the fish. The picture just above it is the heart. The ball is above that one.

items.q: What is next to the star, on its right?
items.e: Just on the right of the star is the ball. The sun is on its left.

items.q: Where is the house? It is ___ the star.
items.e: The house is in the top row, just over the star. So it is above the star.

items.q: What is 2nd from the right?
items.e: Start at the right end and count: 1st is the heart, 2nd is the fish. Counting from the left gives the ball, which is wrong.

items.q: What is in the bottom right corner?
items.e: Bottom means the bottom row. Right means the right side. The bottom right corner is the flower.

items.q: What is between the ball and the house?
items.e: Find the ball and the house. The thing in the middle of them is the fish.

items.q: What is between the fish and the moon?
items.e: Between means in the middle of two things. Go down from the fish to the moon. The picture in the middle is the sun.

items.q: Where is the moon? It is ___ the sun.
items.e: The moon is in the bottom row, just under the sun. So it is below the sun.

items.q: What is in the top left corner?
items.e: Top means the top row. Left means the left side. The top left corner is the fish.

items.q: What is in the middle of the grid?
items.e: The middle square has a picture above it, below it, on its left and on its right. It is the star.

items.q: Where is the star? It is ___ the flower.
items.e: The star and the flower are in the same row. The star is on the left side, so it is on the left of the flower.

items.q: What is just on the right of the sun?
items.e: Look to the right side of the page. Just on the right of the sun is the heart.

items.q: What is on the right of the tree?
items.e: Look to the right side of the page. On the right of the tree is the ball. The moon is on the left.

items.q: What is below the flower?
items.e: Below means lower down. Look down from the flower: the next picture is the ball.

items.q: What is between the star and the flower?
items.e: The thing in the middle of the star and the flower is the ball.

items.q: What is between the sun and the star?
items.e: The sun and the star are in the middle row. The picture between them is the heart.

items.q: What is next to the ball, on its left?
items.e: Next to means right beside it. Just on the left of the ball is the star.

items.q: What is above the sun?
items.e: Above means higher up. Look up from the sun: the next picture is the fish.
The arrow goes halfway round. The end line points the opposite way. That is a half turn.
The arrow goes halfway round, the opposite way to clock hands. That is a half turn anticlockwise.

items.q: The arrow points left. It makes a three-quarter turn clockwise. Which way does it point now?
items.e: Count 3 quarter turns clockwise from left: up, right, down.

items.q: Ava makes a half turn clockwise. Leo makes a half turn anticlockwise. They both start facing the door. What happens?
c: They both face the same way
items.e: A half turn either way makes you face the opposite way. So Ava and Leo end up facing the same way.

items.q: How many right angles make a three-quarter turn?
items.e: A three-quarter turn is 3 quarter turns, so it is 3 right angles.

items.q: Maya faces the sink. She makes a quarter turn clockwise. What does she face now?
items.e: Clockwise goes the same way as clock hands: from the sink round to the door. That is a quarter turn.

items.q: Which turn does the arrow show? It starts at the dashed line.
items.e: The arrow goes a quarter of the way round, the same way as clock hands. That is clockwise.

items.q: What turn does the arrow show? It starts at the dashed line.
items.e: The arrow goes a quarter of the way round. That is a quarter turn.

items.q: Which way do the hands on a clock turn?
items.e: Clock hands always turn the same way. That way is called clockwise. The other way is anticlockwise.

items.q: Aisha faces the door. She makes a half turn. What does she face now?
items.e: A half turn makes you face the opposite way. The board is opposite the door.

items.q: Jack turns through 2 right angles. What turn is that?
items.e: Each right angle is a quarter turn. 2 quarter turns make a half turn.

items.q: Which turn does the arrow show? It starts at the dashed line.
items.e: The arrow goes a quarter of the way round, the opposite way to clock hands. That is anticlockwise.

items.q: How many right angles make a quarter turn?
items.e: A quarter turn is 1 right angle: a square corner.

items.q: How many right angles make a half turn?
items.e: A half turn is 2 quarter turns, so it is 2 right angles.
The arrow goes halfway round, the same way as clock hands. That is a half turn clockwise.

items.q: The arrow points up. It makes a quarter turn anticlockwise. Which way does it point now?
items.e: Anticlockwise goes up, left, down, right. A quarter turn anticlockwise from up is left.
The arrow goes all the way round, back to the dashed line. That is a whole turn.

items.q: The arrow points up. It makes a quarter turn clockwise. Which way does it point now?
items.e: Clockwise goes up, right, down, left. A quarter turn clockwise from up is right.
The arrow goes three quarters of the way round. That is a three-quarter turn.

items.q: The arrow points right. It makes a half turn. Which way does it point now?
items.e: A half turn makes the arrow point the opposite way. The opposite of right is left.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. What will the 12th shape be?
items.e: Each group of 3 ends with a triangle: the 3rd, 6th, 9th and 12th shapes. So the 12th shape is a triangle.

items.q: What comes next in the pattern?
items.e: The part that repeats is circle, triangle, square, triangle. After triangle comes square.

items.q: The arrows make a turning pattern. What comes next?
items.e: Each arrow makes a quarter turn clockwise: right, down, left, up. Next is up.

items.q: How does the arrow turn each time?
items.e: Down to right is a quarter turn the opposite way to clock hands. So each arrow turns a quarter turn anticlockwise.

items.q: How does the arrow turn each time?
items.e: Left to up is a quarter turn the same way as clock hands. So each arrow turns a quarter turn clockwise.

items.q: What comes next in the pattern?
items.e: The part that repeats is triangle, circle, star. After triangle comes circle.

items.q: What comes next in the pattern?
items.e: The part that repeats is heart, heart, circle, circle. The circle comes twice, so the next one is a circle again.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. What will the 10th shape be?
items.e: Keep counting the pattern: 7 star, 8 heart, 9 circle, 10 star.

items.q: What comes next in the pattern?
items.e: The part that repeats is square, square, heart. The square comes twice, so the next one is a square again.

items.q: The arrows make a turning pattern. What comes next?
items.e: Each arrow makes a quarter turn clockwise: up, right, down, left. Next is left.

items.q: What comes next in the pattern?
items.e: The part that repeats is circle, square. After circle comes square.

items.q: What is missing from the pattern?
items.e: The pattern repeats square, triangle, triangle. Say it along the row: the gap needs triangle.

items.q: Which part of the pattern repeats?
items.e: Circle, circle, star, then it starts again: circle, circle, star.
The pattern repeats heart, star, square. Say it along the row: the gap needs square.

items.q: One shape is wrong in this pattern. Which one?
items.e: The pattern is triangle, star, circle. Shape 6 should be a circle, but it is a star.

items.q: The arrows make a turning pattern. What comes next?
items.e: Each arrow makes a quarter turn anticlockwise: up, left, down, right. Next is right.

items.q: The arrows make a turning pattern. What comes next?
items.e: Each arrow makes a half turn: up, down, up, down. After up comes down.

items.q: What is missing from the pattern?
items.e: The pattern repeats star, circle. Say it along the row: the gap needs circle.

items.q: Jack makes a pattern: circle, square, square. He keeps going until there are 9 shapes. How many squares are there?
items.e: 9 shapes make 3 groups of circle, square, square. Each group has 2 squares. 2 + 2 + 2 = 6.
The part that repeats is star, heart, heart. After heart comes star.

sets.title: Moving on a grid: forwards, backwards and turns

items.q: The robot faces up the page. It goes forwards 3, turn left, forwards 2. Where does it stop?
items.e: Go forwards 3 first. Turning left makes the robot face left. Then go forwards 2.

items.q: The robot faces down the page. It goes forwards 3. Where does it stop?
items.e: Move 3 squares down, one square at a time. Do not count the square the robot starts on.

items.q: The robot faces down the page. It goes forwards 2, turn left, forwards 2. Where does it stop?
items.e: The robot faces down the page, so its left is on the right of the page. Turn the page upside down to check. Go forwards 2, turn left (towards the right of the page), then forwards 2.

items.q: The robot faces right. How many squares must it go forwards to reach the star?
items.e: Count the moves, not the robot’s own square. 4 squares forwards takes the robot to the star.

items.q: The robot faces down the page. It goes forwards 3, turn right, forwards 2. Where does it stop?
items.e: The robot faces down the page, so its right is on the left of the page. Turn the page upside down to check. Go forwards 3, turn right (towards the left of the page), then forwards 2.

items.q: The robot faces right. What must it do to face the star?
items.e: The star is behind the robot. A half turn makes it face the opposite way.

items.q: The robot faces right. It goes backwards 2. Where does it stop?
items.e: Backwards means the robot moves the opposite way to where it faces, without turning. Move 2 squares to the left.

items.q: The robot faces down the page. Which instructions take it to the star?
items.e: Go down 2 squares. The robot faces down the page, so turning right makes it face the left of the page. Then go 3 squares.

items.q: The robot faces down the page. What must it do to face the star?
items.e: The robot faces down the page, so its left is on the right of the page. It turns left to face the star.

items.q: The robot faces left. It goes forwards 2, turn left, forwards 2. Where does it stop?
items.e: Go forwards 2 first. Turning left makes the robot face down the page. Then go forwards 2.

items.q: The robot faces up the page. Which instructions take it to the star?
items.e: Go up 2 squares. Turn right to face the right of the page. Then go 4 squares to reach the star.

items.q: The robot faces left. It goes forwards 2. Where does it stop?
items.e: Move 2 squares to the left, one square at a time. Do not count the square the robot starts on.

items.q: The robot faces up the page. It goes forwards 3. Where does it stop?
items.e: Move 3 squares up, one square at a time. Do not count the square the robot starts on.

items.q: The robot faces left. How many squares must it go forwards to reach the star?
items.e: Count the moves, not the robot’s own square. 2 squares forwards takes the robot to the star.

items.q: The robot faces right. It goes forwards 3, turn right, forwards 2. Where does it stop?
items.e: Go forwards 3 first. Turning right makes the robot face down the page. Then go forwards 2.

items.q: The robot faces up the page. It goes forwards 2, turn right, forwards 3. Where does it stop?
items.e: Go forwards 2 first. Turning right makes the robot face right. Then go forwards 3.

items.q: The robot faces up the page. It goes backwards 2. Where does it stop?
items.e: Backwards means the robot moves the opposite way to where it faces, without turning. Move 2 squares down.

items.q: The robot faces down the page. How many squares must it go forwards to reach the star?
items.e: Count the moves, not the robot’s own square. 3 squares forwards takes the robot to the star.

items.q: The robot faces right. It goes forwards 3. Where does it stop?
items.e: Move 3 squares to the right, one square at a time. Do not count the square the robot starts on.

items.q: The robot faces up the page. What must it do to face the star?
items.e: The robot faces up the page. The star is on its right side, so it turns right: a quarter turn clockwise.

sets.title: Real-life problems: maps, robots and the playground

items.q: How do you get from the pond to the flag?
items.e: From the pond, go 1 square left and 2 squares up to reach the flag. Do not count the square you start on.

items.q: Start at the flag. Go 2 squares left and 2 squares down. What do you find?
items.e: From the flag, go 2 squares left and 2 squares down. You reach the house.

items.q: Five children stand in a line. Who is between Kai and Noah?
items.e: Find Kai and Noah. Ruby is in the middle of them.

items.q: Ava faces the slide. She makes a quarter turn anticlockwise. What does she face now?
items.e: Anticlockwise is the opposite way to clock hands. A quarter turn anticlockwise from the slide is the swings.

items.q: Who is just on the right of Ruby in the picture?
items.e: Look to the right side of the page. Next to Ruby on that side is Noah. Kai is on her left.

items.q: The minute hand turns clockwise from the dashed line. What turn has it made?
items.e: From 12 to 6 is halfway round the clock: a half turn.

items.q: Oliver’s toy robot faces left. It goes forwards 2, turn right, forwards 1. Where does it stop?
items.e: Go 2 squares to the left. The robot faces left, so turning right makes it face up the page. Then go 1 square up.

items.q: Poppy programs a toy robot. It faces up the page. It goes forwards 3, turn left, forwards 2. Where does it stop?
items.e: Go up 3 squares. Turning left makes the robot face the left of the page. Then go 2 squares.
From 12 to 9 is 3 quarters of the way round: 12 to 3, 3 to 6, 6 to 9. That is a three-quarter turn.

items.q: George faces the sandpit. He makes a half turn. What does he face now?
items.e: A half turn makes you face the opposite way. The slide is opposite the sandpit.

items.q: Ruby faces the board. She turns round to face the back wall. What turn has she made?
items.e: The back wall is opposite the board. Turning to face the opposite way is a half turn.

items.q: Isla spins round in the playground until she faces the same way again. What turn is that?
items.e: Facing the same way again means going all the way round: a whole turn (4 right angles).

items.q: You walk forwards and turn right. Which way have you turned?
items.e: Turning right is a quarter turn the same way as clock hands: clockwise. Turning left is anticlockwise.

items.q: Zara puts beads on a string: round, round, square, round, round, square. What is the 10th bead?
items.e: The beads repeat in groups of 3: round, round, square. The 9th bead is square, so the 10th starts a new group: round.

items.q: Who is 4th from the left?
items.e: Count from the left: Ava 1st, Kai 2nd, Ruby 3rd, Noah 4th. Counting from the right gives Kai.

items.q: Start at the house. Go 2 squares right and 2 squares down. What do you find?
items.e: From the house, go 2 squares right and 2 squares down. You reach the treasure chest.

items.q: Kai faces the swings. He makes a quarter turn clockwise. What does he face now?
items.e: Clockwise is the way clock hands go. A quarter turn clockwise from the swings is the slide.

items.q: Bunting has flags that point down, up, down, up. What does the 9th flag do?
items.e: The odd flags (1st, 3rd, 5th, 7th, 9th) point down. The even flags point up.

items.q: How do you get from the house to the treasure chest?
items.e: From the house, go 2 squares right and 2 squares down to reach the treasure chest. Do not count the square you start on.

items.q: Start at the tent. Go 1 square up and 2 squares left. What do you find?
items.e: From the tent, go 1 square up and 2 squares left. You reach the pond.
